collections.name: policies
collections.description: Published BRMS policies that executions are associated with. Kept as a separate collection because policies are reusable across many execution requests and are needed for policy-version analytics.

fields.name: policy_id
fields.description: Stable business identifier from BRMS.

fields.name: version
fields.description: Published policy version used for impact analysis.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Included because policy lifecycle is part of broader product context, though POV focuses on execution logs.

fields.name: consolidated_input_schema
fields.description: Optional summary of consolidated input expected by the policy; supports FR13 without over-modeling authoring workflows.

fields.name: rule_refs
fields.description: References to reusable rule definitions associated with this policy version.

relationships.description: A policy version can have many execution requests.

embedding_vs_references.why: Rules are reusable definitions and can be numerous; executions only need policy/rule identifiers, while analytics may join by identifiers. Keeping policy metadata separate avoids duplicating policy details on every execution request, while still snapshotting policy version info onto requests for read efficiency.

indexes.name: ux_policy_business_key
indexes.reason: Supports lookup of a specific published policy version and ensures uniqueness for analytics grouped by policy version (UC3, FR13).

indexes.name: idx_policy_status
indexes.reason: Supports listing/filtering policies by lifecycle state for product-context demos around published policies (UC4, FR13).

collections.name: rules
collections.description: Rule definitions referenced by policies and execution steps. Separate collection because rules are reused across many requests and are useful for rule-level analytics.

fields.name: rule_id
fields.description: Stable business identifier from BRMS.

fields.name: policy_id
fields.description: Owning policy business identifier.

fields.name: sequence
fields.description: Execution/display ordering within a policy when applicable.

fields.name: is_lookup_enabled
fields.description: Whether runtime DB lookup can occur for this rule when configured (FR15).

relationships.description: Rules belong to a policy version.
Execution steps reference rule identifiers executed for a request.

embedding_vs_references.decision: store rule definitions separately, but snapshot key rule attributes into execution steps
embedding_vs_references.why: Execution reads need fast request reconstruction without joins, so step documents carry rule_id/rule_name/sequence snapshots. Separate rules collection supports policy/rule catalogs and analytics dimensions without bloating policy docs.

indexes.name: ux_rule_business_key
indexes.reason: Supports unique lookup of a specific rule definition version and correlation from step records (UC1, UC3).

indexes.name: idx_rule_policy
indexes.reason: Supports listing rules for a policy/version in evaluation order (FR13, UC1).

collections.name: execution_requests
collections.description: Primary audit document for each request/correlation ID. Stores request/response JSON and embedded rule-level steps to support request-centric retrieval and detailed audit review.

fields.name: tenant_id
fields.description: Optional customer/environment identifier because tenant isolation is an open question, but customer-specific logging/retention exists.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description: Business request/correlation identifier used to retrieve all rule information for a request (FR10).

fields.name: correlation_id
fields.description: Optional separate correlation ID when different from request_id.

fields.name: invocation_channel
fields.description: Captures source application context implied by integrations/use cases.

fields.name: logging_enabled
fields.description: Whether detailed execution logging was enabled for this request/customer context (FR18).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Supports asynchronous/incremental ingestion lifecycle (FR5, FR6).

fields.name: final_outcome
fields.description: High-level business result such as approved/rejected/eligible/ineligible used in analytics.

fields.name: outcome_reason_codes
fields.description: Normalized reasons for approval/rejection when available, supporting audit and analytics.

fields.name: request_payload
fields.description: Full nested input JSON; supports complex arrays/nesting (FR1, FR4, FR14).

fields.name: response_payload
fields.description: Final output JSON returned to consuming app (FR1, FR12).

fields.name: payload_summary
fields.description: Optional extracted top-level fields/metrics used frequently in dashboards to avoid repeated deep JSON traversal.

fields.name: rule_step_count
fields.description: Number of logged rule steps, supports monitoring of variable step volumes (FR3, FR20).

fields.name: rule_steps
fields.description: Embedded chronological rule execution details for the request.

fields.name: stage_name
fields.description: Stage within rule execution, e.g. initiation, stage1, stage2.

fields.name: input_snapshot
fields.description: Intermediate input/state at this step.

fields.name: output_snapshot
fields.description: Intermediate output/state at this step.

fields.name: decision
fields.description: Step-level decision or result if present.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Human-readable explanation when available.

fields.name: lookup_details
fields.description: Optional metadata about runtime DB lookup performed by the rule (FR15).

fields.name: ingestion_metadata
fields.description: Supports asynchronous ingestion traceability from Kafka/queue pathways (FR5, INT1).

fields.name: retention
expire_at
fields.description: Per-document retention cutoff to support purging/TTL (FR19).
Retention controls driven by customer needs and growth management.

relationships.description: Each request executes one policy version.
A request contains multiple chronological rule execution step logs.

embedding_vs_references.why: The dominant access pattern is request-centric audit retrieval by request/correlation ID showing full request, response, and all internal steps together (UC1, FR10). Step counts are variable but typically tens to low hundreds per request, making embedding appropriate for the POV and simplifying atomic request reconstruction. Separate per-step collection is avoided unless real volumes approach document limits.

indexes.name: ux_request_id
indexes.reason: Primary retrieval path for audit investigation by request ID/correlation ID (UJ1, UC1, FR10).

indexes.name: idx_correlation_id
indexes.reason: Supports retrieval when clients use a correlation ID distinct from request ID (FR10, review ISSUE-3).

indexes.name: idx_policy_version_time_outcome
indexes.reason: Supports policy-version impact analytics over time and approval/rejection comparisons (UC3, BO3, BO4, FR17).

indexes.name: idx_status_time
indexes.reason: Supports monitoring incremental/asynchronous ingestion and recent failed/in-progress requests (FR5, FR6, FR7).

indexes.name: idx_retention_expire_at
indexes.reason: Supports retention management and TTL-style purging workflows (UC5, FR19).

indexes.name: idx_tenant_policy_time
indexes.reason: Supports customer-scoped analytics and operational filtering where tenant/customer separation is needed (FR18, UC2, UC3).

indexes.name: search_logged_content
indexes.reason: Supports fast search/filtering within nested JSON content and rule-step data, which is a core pain point in the current relational approach (UC2, FR16, MO2).

collections.name: analytics_daily_policy_outcomes
collections.description: Pre-aggregated daily metrics by policy version and outcome to power dashboards efficiently. Included because dashboard/reporting is a stated requirement, while remaining secondary to the raw audit log model.

fields.name: other_outcome_counts
fields.description: Flexible counts for outcomes beyond approved/rejected.

relationships.description: Precomputed from raw execution request data for dashboard speed.

embedding_vs_references.why: Dashboard/report workloads differ from raw audit retrieval. Pre-aggregating avoids repeatedly scanning large execution payloads for common management views while preserving raw logs as source of truth.

indexes.name: ux_daily_policy_metric
indexes.reason: Supports dashboard queries over time by tenant and policy version and prevents duplicate daily metric rows (UC3, FR17).

indexes.name: idx_policy_metric_date
indexes.reason: Supports trend charts comparing policy versions over time (UC3, BO4).
